label: DORA + AMLA + NIS2 Integration Orchestrator
description: Stitches DORA, AMLA/AMLR and NIS2 into ONE programme: a shared ICT/asset inventory, an overlap-vs-distinct obligations matrix, a reconciled incident-reporting timeline, unified third-party registers, and a single sequenced roadmap — not three parallel projects.

claudeKnowledge.description: DORA (EU) 2022/2554 + ESA RTS/ITS, AMLR (EU) 2024/1624, AMLA Reg (EU) 2024/1620, AMLD6 (EU) 2024/1640, NIS2 Dir (EU) 2022/2555 + national transposition, MiCA (EU) 2023/1114, TFR (EU) 2023/1113

guidedInputs.label: Known concerns, conflicts or audit findings
guidedInputs.description: Describe known tensions between the regimes, prior findings, or specific reconciliation pain points.
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. The same Azure tenancy is in our DORA Register of Information but absent from the NIS2 supply-chain list; ICT incident escalation runs to the CISO while STR escalation runs to the MLRO with no shared trigger; the DORA Register of Information and the AMLR outsourcing register are maintained on different spreadsheets by different teams; a Q3 supervisory letter questioned why a ransomware event was reported to the national CSIRT but not assessed for STR implications.

exampleInput: We are a Swedish payment institution (~250 staff, e-money licence, ~80% of volume on a single cloud provider) that has just realised we are simultaneously in scope for DORA, AMLR/AMLA and the Swedish NIS2 transposition (Cybersäkerhetslagen). Today these run as three separate projects: a DORA workstream owned by IT resilience, an AMLR readiness programme owned by the MLRO, and a NIS2 project owned by the CISO. They use different asset lists, different third-party registers, and have never reconciled their incident-reporting clocks. Last quarter a ransomware incident on our KYC vendor was reported to the national CSIRT under NIS2, classified as a major ICT incident under DORA, but nobody assessed whether the compromised customer data also created an STR/SAR obligation — and our board got three different incident narratives. Build us the integrated picture: one critical-asset and ICT/data inventory, a matrix showing which obligations overlap versus which are distinct across the three regimes, a single reconciled incident-reporting timeline that places the DORA initial/intermediate/final reports, the NIS2 24h early-warning / 72h notification / 1-month final, and any STR filing on one clock with a shared trigger, a single third-party register that satisfies the DORA Article 28 Register of Information, AMLR outsourcing oversight, and NIS2 supply-chain requirements at once, a reconciled board attestation order, and one sequenced roadmap. We do NOT want three parallel programmes.

exampleValues.known_concerns: Same cloud tenancy appears in the DORA Register of Information but not the NIS2 supply-chain list. ICT incident escalation runs to the CISO; STR escalation runs to the MLRO; no shared trigger. A KYC-vendor ransomware event was reported to the CSIRT and classified as a major ICT incident, but never assessed for STR implications. Board received three divergent incident narratives.
